title: Minimum Absolute Difference
summary: Given an array of distinct integers, identify all pairs with the smallest difference between any two numbers.
statement: Given an array of distinct integers, identify all pairs with the smallest difference between any two numbers. Return a sorted list of these pairs, where each pair consists of two distinct numbers from the array, with the first number less than the second, and the difference between them is the minimum possible.
constraints: Return ascending pairs in ascending order.
reference_solution:
def minimum_absolute_pairs(arr):
 arr=sorted(arr);gap=min(b-a for a,b in zip(arr,arr[1:]));return [[a,b] for a,b in zip(arr,arr[1:]) if b-a==gap]
hints: Only adjacent values in sorted order can attain the global minimum difference.
Sort, compute the smallest neighboring gap, then collect every neighbor pair with that gap.
Emit pairs during a second neighboring scan.
Any nonadjacent sorted pair spans at least one neighboring gap and cannot be smaller than all of them.
editorial: Any nonadjacent sorted pair spans at least one neighboring gap and cannot be smaller than all of them.

tests.explanation: After sorting, every adjacent gap is one, so all three neighboring pairs qualify.
The unique minimum gap is two between one and three.
